issue.title: sase-core-rs floor is 0.26.10 (<0.27.0) but task wire schema v2 shipped in 0.27.0, failing 64 tests in the tasks/task-handler subsystem
issue.description:
Reproduction in workspace sase_16 (host project gh_sase-org__sase) on 2026-08-13 while
running `SASE_CORE_DIR=<workspace-linked-sase-core> just check-full` (unrelated to the
change being landed, a notification-panel feature):

    64 failed, 29736 passed, 10 skipped
    FAILED tests/main/test_task_handler_kill.py (3 tests)
    FAILED tests/main/test_task_handler_list.py (10 tests)
    FAILED tests/main/test_task_handler_run.py (11 tests)
    FAILED tests/main/test_task_handler_show.py (7 tests)
    FAILED tests/test_tasks_facade.py (3 tests)
    FAILED tests/test_tasks_runner.py (13 tests)
    FAILED tests/ace/tui/test_task_mirror.py (6 tests)
    FAILED tests/ace/tui/test_tasks_store_rows.py (5 tests)
    FAILED tests/ace/tui/test_app_title.py::test_on_mount_keeps_initial_title_when_resolver_returns_none

Isolated repro (project venv, fresh temp SASE_HOME per test):

    $ python -m pytest tests/test_tasks_runner.py::test_submit_supervisor_captures_output_and_task_environment -q
    sase.tasks.runner.TaskSubmitError: could not record task: task wire schema
    mismatch: got 2, expected 1
        src/sase/tasks/runner.py:152: in _submit_supervised_task
            raise TaskSubmitError(...) from exc

Root cause: src/sase/tasks/models.py:11 hardcodes
`TASK_WIRE_SCHEMA_VERSION: Final = 1` and models.py:256-259 raises when the
value the sase_core_rs binding reports does not match. pyproject.toml:46 /
uv.lock cap sase-core-rs at `>=0.26.10,<0.27.0`, but the linked sase-core
checkout (up to date with origin/master, not stale -- `git status` there
shows "up to date with 'origin/master'") builds and installs 0.27.0
(confirmed via `python -c "import importlib.metadata as m;
print(m.version('sase-core-rs'))"` => 0.27.0). 0.27.0 ships task wire schema
version 2; the Python-side floor/schema constant was never bumped to match,
so every task-store write (append_task -> _submit_supervised_task) fails
immediately in any environment that resolves the real published 0.27.0
(not just this workspace's linked-repo override).

Same recurring class as sase-h0, sase-hz, sase-jj, sase-ic, sase-d7, sase-cn
(sase-core-rs floor lags a feature that already shipped in the next published
version) -- not workspace drift like the canceled sase-jw, since the linked
checkout here is current with origin/master, and the mismatch reproduces
against the plain installed package version, not a stale build artifact.

Fix likely needs two coordinated parts: raise pyproject.toml's sase-core-rs
floor to >=0.27.0 (or the correct minimum that carries the task schema v2
change), and update src/sase/tasks/models.py's TASK_WIRE_SCHEMA_VERSION
(and any schema-version handling around it) to accept/produce schema 2.

Verified as unrelated to the notification_read_current_tab plan being
implemented alongside this: the failing files are entirely in the
tasks/task-handler/task-mirror subsystem, none touch notifications, and the
focused notification test suite (69 tests across
tests/notification_store/test_state_updates.py,
tests/test_core_facade/test_notification_store.py,
tests/test_notification_modal_action_bindings.py,
tests/test_notification_modal_mark_and_tabs.py,
tests/test_notification_modal_read_tab.py) plus the 13
notification-touching PNG visual snapshots all pass.

evidence.note: Independent reproduction by sase-ky.land in workspace sase_11 (host project gh_sase-org__sase), 2026-08-13, at HEAD 4183f3d4d. After 'sase repo open sase-core' updated the workspace-linked checkout to origin/master (5b8ba44, tag v0.27.0) and 'just install' built sase-core-rs 0.27.0 from it, 'just check' failed 69 tests -- the same subsystem set as the sase_16 report plus tests/notification_store/test_state_updates.py::TestMarkTabRead (5 nodes) and tests/test_core_facade/test_notification_store.py (those 6 are a SEPARATE defect, see sase-ln). Same error: 'ValueError: task wire schema mismatch: got 2, expected 1' at src/sase/tasks/models.py:257. CONFIRMED FIX DIRECTION: checking the linked sase-core checkout out at tag v0.26.11 and rerunning 'just install' (installed sase-core-rs 0.26.11) drops those 63 task-subsystem failures to zero, which isolates the cause to the 0.27.0 wire bump rather than to anything in the repo's Python. NOTE FOR WHOEVER WORKS THIS: 'sase repo open sase-core' always updates the linked checkout to origin/master, and the Justfile prefers that checkout over the published wheel, so every SASE agent that opens sase-core now installs 0.27.0 and inherits these 63 failures. RELATED: epic sase-lh (Rename SASE Background Tasks to Procs) is the in-progress owner of the Python-side migration to the new core; its phase sase-lh.2 covers the package move.

Independently reproduced by epic sase-l6 phase sase-l6.5 (2026-08-13T22:43:06Z): just check's test-scoped lane failed 63 pre-existing tests (tests/main/test_task_handler_*.py, tests/ace/tui/test_task_mirror.py, tests/ace/tui/test_tasks_store_rows.py, tests/test_tasks_facade.py, tests/test_tasks_runner.py) with 'TaskSubmitError: could not record task: task wire schema mismatch: got 2, expected 1'. Reproduced identically on a clean git stash (no sase-l6.5 changes applied), confirming it is a pre-existing sase-core-rs floor/wire-schema mismatch in that workspace state, not caused by that phase. Not currently reproducing in workspace sase_11 as of the sase-l6.6 land pass (2026-08-14): 'just check' passed clean there, consistent with this task's own finding that the linked sase-core checkout version in use determines whether the mismatch triggers.

payload.entry: Triage sweep 2026-08-14 (master 443566f7d, workspace sase_13): the tasks/task-handler suites named here were renamed by the procs work (tests/test_tasks_facade.py -> tests/test_procs_facade.py, tests/test_tasks_runner.py -> tests/test_procs_runner.py) and now pass: 38 passed. pyproject.toml still pins sase-core-rs>=0.26.10,<0.27.0 while the linked sase-core checkout is 0.27.0, but tools/validate_sase_core_rs_version now reports that explicitly as expected ('editable installs build from the checkout regardless, and tools/ratchet_core_window moves the published window on the release branch at release time'). The generic gap this exposed -- floor gates that check binding names but not wire schema versions -- remains tracked by sase-km.

payload.close_reason: No longer reproducible; the affected suites pass and the window mismatch is the expected dev-install state.

payload.entry: Correction to the close note above: sase-km was itself closed in the same 2026-08-14 triage sweep (deprioritized as preventive, not stale -- the wire-schema gap in tools/probe_core_floor and tools/check_sase_core_rs_bindings is still real). So the generic floor-vs-schema gate is no longer tracked by an open bead; re-file via a +1 on sase-km at the next real mismatch.

evidence.note: Independent corroboration on 2026-08-14 while verifying provider-qualified model completion: main repo 'just check' printed core-floor-probe status stale_actionable for declared floor 0.26.10, missing published v0.27.0 proc capabilities append_proc, prune_procs, read_procs_snapshot, and update_proc. The check lane continued and passed, but the floor drift is still live on this workspace.
